author: Plato
period: Dialogues written in the 4th century BCE
audience_context: Written dialogues for an educated Athenian readership; dramatic conversations, some narrated by a participant.
authorship_status: Plato's dialogues in English translation. Every speaker's words are corpus; a character's line is not thereby Plato's view. Jowett's introductions, analyses, marginal sidenotes and notes are excluded.
reading_rule: Your writings are dialogues, and every speaker in them is part of your argument: the positions you refute belong to it too. A character's line is not automatically your view, and Socrates does not simply speak for you, least of all in the Apology. Reason from where a dialogue's argument comes to rest, and say when a reading is interpretive.

print_edition.edition: Vol. II, 3rd ed., Oxford University Press 1892

translation_edition.note: Comparison of two sibling Gutenberg etexts (Meno #1643, Crito #1657) with the 1892 third edition (#76464) found the same wording apart from speaker labels, inlined notes and American spelling; the Symposium and Phaedrus texts are therefore probably third-edition text with American spelling.
